newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Hochtief current year sales up so far.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hochtief current year sales up so far.

text.p: German construction group Hochtief said on Thursday group sales for the first five months of the year rose 5.4 percent to 4.7 billion marks ($2.7 billion), largely due to international business.

Hochtief, Germany's second largest builder after Philipp Holzmann AG, also told an annual shareholders meeting it was now holding "concrete talks" on possible cooperation with Holzmann in foreign markets.

The two earlier this month had to call off a planned equity deal that would have seen Hochtief's current 24.9 percent stake in Holzmann rise to nearly 50 percent after German cartel authorities made it clear they would block the deal.

"Hochtief will, within the narrow framework set out by German cartel law, nonetheless study areas of cooperation to confront the concentration taking place in the building sectors of neighbouring countries," Hochtief chief Hans-Peter Keitel said.

Hochtief, which saw incoming orders from January to May rise 2.8 percent to 5.2 billion and its order book swell to 13.8 billion marks, up 17.4 pct on the year, said its international business was becoming increasingly important.

Its Australian-based Leighton Holdings, South African Concor Ltd and Dutch Ballast Nedam all maintained or increased their profit contributions compared to the previous year, Hochtief said. Precise breakdowns were not given.
Hochtief also said it was confident of being among a small group of candidates with a chance to buy a 50 percent stake in Duesseldorf airport project.
"We are assuming, that Hochtief will be the only firm from North Rhine-Westphalia with experience in international airports to be able to work out a binding offer," Keitel said.
North Rhine-Westphalia is the central German state in which the airport is located.
Eight bids have currently been made to buy a 50 percent stake in the airport. The offers are scheduled to be narrowed down to just two or three by the beginning of July.
The remaining 50 percent of the airport is held by the city of Duesseldorf.
